stories.headline: ARC-AGI-3 Launches as Interactive Benchmark, Frontier LLMs Score Below 1%

key_facts.fact: ARC-AGI-3 launched on March 25, 2026 as a fundamentally new benchmark that abandons static grid puzzles for interactive, video-game-like environments where AI agents must discover rules and solve problems with zero instructions.
Frontier LLMs including GPT-5 and Claude score below 1%, while simple CNN and graph-search approaches reach 12.58%, with human performance at 100%.
The competition carries over $2 million in prizes across three tracks, with $700K grand prize for a 100% score and submissions due November 2, 2026.
The benchmark contains 1,000+ levels across 150+ handcrafted environments, where agents enter 64x64 grid worlds with 16 colors and must learn through trial-and-error.
ARC-AGI-3 measures intelligence across time, not just final answers, capturing planning horizons, memory compression, and the ability to update beliefs as new evidence appears.

stories.headline: Google Introduces TurboQuant: 6x LLM Memory Reduction and 8x Speedup at Zero Accuracy Loss

key_facts.fact: Google Research published TurboQuant, a data-oblivious quantization framework that compresses LLM key-value caches to 3 bits per value, reducing memory by 6x and delivering up to 8x speedup with no accuracy loss.

TurboQuant combines PolarQuant, which converts Cartesian vectors to polar coordinates eliminating normalization overhead, with QJL which reduces residual errors to single sign bits with zero memory overhead.
The algorithm was tested on Gemma and Mistral models running on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, achieving up to 8x performance boost over unquantized keys.
TurboQuant is data-oblivious, requiring no dataset-specific calibration for deployment, and was validated across LongBench, Needle In A Haystack, ZeroSCROLLS, RULER, and L-Eval benchmarks.
The compression enables powerful AI models to run locally on consumer devices like a 16GB Mac Mini or smartphones, according to coverage.

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Auto Mode for Claude Code, Letting AI Make Permission Decisions

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released auto mode for Claude Code on March 24, 2026 as a research preview, placing it between babysitting every action and the risky --dangerously-skip-permissions flag.

A built-in classifier reviews each tool call before execution, scanning for mass file deletions, data exfiltration attempts, malicious code execution, and prompt injection, blocking risky actions automatically.
The feature is available now for Team plan users with rollout to Enterprise and API users in coming days, and is compatible with Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6 models.
Auto mode is disabled by default on the desktop app and requires admin settings for CLI and VS Code; Anthropic recommends use in isolated environments due to potential false positives.

stories.headline: OpenAI Foundation Pledges $1B in Grants, Names Zaremba to Lead AI Resilience

key_facts.fact: The OpenAI Foundation committed to investing at least $1 billion in grants over the next year across four program areas: life sciences, jobs and economic impact, AI resilience, and community programs.
OpenAI co-founder Wojciech Zaremba is joining the Foundation to lead the AI Resilience program, and Robert Kaiden (ex-Deloitte, Twitter, Inspirato) joins as CFO.
The Foundation's spending represents a massive pivot: the nonprofit listed only $7.6 million in grants in 2024 and $3.3 million in expenses in 2019, making the $1B pledge a 130x increase.

Life sciences lead Jacob Trefethen previously oversaw $500M+ in grantmaking at Coefficient Giving; the program will target Alzheimer's research and high-mortality disease acceleration using AI-assisted drug discovery.

The $1B is an early tranche of the $25 billion commitment the Foundation announced in October when OpenAI completed its recapitalization into a public benefit corporation valued at approximately $130 billion.

stories.headline: LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack Steals SSH Keys and Cloud Credentials From 95M-Download Package

key_facts.fact: On March 24, 2026, LiteLLM PyPI versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were published with credential-stealing malware via a compromised maintainer account, part of the broader TeamPCP supply chain campaign.

The malicious .pth file auto-executed on every Python invocation without any import, stealing environment variables, SSH private keys, AWS/GCP/Azure/Kubernetes credentials, git configs, shell history, and crypto wallet files.
LiteLLM has approximately 95 million monthly downloads on PyPI and serves as a dependency for major AI frameworks including DSPy and CrewAI, amplifying the attack's blast radius.

Datadog's investigation traced the attack to a five-day TeamPCP campaign that began with the March 19 Trivy compromise, continued through CanisterWorm on npm, then hit Checkmarx KICS before reaching LiteLLM.
The attack was discovered accidentally when a developer's machine crashed from RAM exhaustion caused by a bug in the malware that triggered an exponential fork bomb.
PyPI quarantined the entire litellm package and LiteLLM is pausing new releases until completing a broader supply-chain review.

stories.headline: OpenAI Publishes Model Spec Philosophy, the 100-Page Framework Governing ChatGPT

key_facts.fact: On March 25, 2026, OpenAI published a detailed blog post explaining the philosophy and mechanics behind its Model Spec, the 100-page document that defines how ChatGPT should behave across all queries.

The Model Spec defines how models should follow instructions, resolve conflicts, respect user freedom, and behave safely, functioning both as a description of current behavior and a target for improvement.

OpenAI frames the document as an interface so that researchers, policymakers, and the public can read, inspect, and debate intended model behavior rather than it being hidden inside the training process.

stories.headline: Meta Reorganizes 1,000-Person Reality Labs Team Into AI-Native Pods

key_facts.fact: Meta Reality Labs is reorganizing a 1,000-employee developer tools team into AI-native pods, replacing traditional roles with three titles: AI Builder, AI Pod Lead, and AI Org Lead.
The restructuring aims to create a flatter organization focused on engineering productivity and product quality, a structure that CEO Mark Zuckerberg has advocated.
Meta said the AI-native pod restructuring is unrelated to the approximately 700 layoffs it carried out on March 25 across Facebook, Global Operations, Recruiting, and other divisions.
The pod structure is part of Meta's broader AI-first push, which includes $115-135 billion in capital expenditure budgeted for 2026, primarily for AI servers and data center infrastructure.

stories.headline: Figure AI Founder Launches Hark AI Lab With $100M and Apple's iPhone Air Designer

key_facts.fact: Brett Adcock, CEO of $39 billion humanoid robotics company Figure AI, publicly launched Hark with $100 million of his own money, hiring 45 engineers from Apple, Meta, Google, and Tesla.
Hark's most notable hire is Abidur Chowdhury, the industrial designer who led Apple's iPhone Air team and presented the device at Apple's keynote, now serving as Director of Design.

Hark is building end-to-end speech, text, and vision models with persistent memory alongside custom AI hardware devices, planning to ship first AI models by summer 2026 and scale to 100 employees by mid-year.

Chowdhury expressed skepticism about current AI wearables including pins and face-mounted cameras, saying Hark's philosophy centers on removing barriers between intelligence and users rather than adding gadgets.

stories.headline: Anthropic Economic Index: Experienced AI Users Tackle Higher-Value Tasks With Better Success

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's March 2026 Economic Index report, studying Claude usage from February 5-12, found that high-tenure users (6+ months) demonstrate 4-5 percentage point higher conversation success rates than newer users.
Usage on Claude.ai diversified significantly: the top 10 tasks declined from 24% to 19% of conversations between November 2025 and February 2026, while personal use increased from 35% to 42%.
The rate of augmentation (collaborative AI-human interaction) increased slightly in both Claude.ai and API traffic, continuing the trend that augmentation outpaces pure automation.
For every $10 increase in hourly wage of the task, Opus model usage rises 1.5 percentage points on Claude.ai and 2.8 points on API, indicating users select more powerful models for higher-value work.

stories.headline: Judge Says Pentagon's 'Supply Chain Risk' Designation Looks Like Attempt to 'Cripple' Anthropic

key_facts.fact: California District Judge Rita Lin stated on March 25 that the Defense Department's actions against Anthropic 'look like an attempt to cripple' the company, suggesting the designation may be illegal.

The Trump administration had designated Anthropic a 'supply chain risk' for its stance on AI weapons regulation, specifically its insistence that AI products not be deployed for autonomous weapons or domestic surveillance without human oversight.
Anthropic is the first US company to receive such a supply chain risk designation, which would cancel both direct government contracts and those of government contractors using Anthropic products.

Anthropic challenged the ban as violating freedom of speech and due process rights, with the hearing indicating a potential preliminary injunction that could prevent billions in lost government contracts.

stories.headline: NASA Unveils $20B Moon Base Plan, Cancels Lunar Gateway Space Station

key_facts.fact: NASA canceled the Lunar Gateway orbital station and will redirect its components toward a $20 billion base on the moon's surface over seven years.

The base will be built in three phases: Phase 1 (2026-28) focuses on robotic missions and scouting south pole sites, Phase 2 (2029-31) begins construction with two crewed missions per year, Phase 3 (2032+) enables sustained human presence.
NASA plans to launch a nuclear-powered spacecraft called Space Reactor 1 Freedom to Mars before end of 2028, demonstrating advanced nuclear electric propulsion in deep space.
NASA foresees spending $10 billion each on Phases 1 and 2, with Phase 3 costing an additional $10 billion or more through at least 2036.
Administrator Jared Isaacman made the announcement at the 'Ignition' event at NASA headquarters on March 24, as the U.S. races to return to the moon before China sends astronauts there around 2030.
The plan includes deploying a fleet of drones and laying groundwork for using nuclear power on the lunar surface in the next few years.

stories.headline: Isar Aerospace Spectrum Second Flight Scrubbed by Automated Abort at T-0

key_facts.fact: The automated launch abort system activated at T-0 on March 25, preventing engine ignition after the range was initially not ready to support the launch, extending the countdown.

The 'Onward and Upward' mission was Spectrum's qualification flight carrying six ESA-backed payloads from universities and companies including TU Berlin, University of Maribor, EnduroSat, NTNU, TU Wien, and Dcubed.
Spectrum is a two-stage launch vehicle standing 28 meters tall with ten engines, targeting payloads up to 1,000 kg to low Earth orbit, at an estimated price of EUR 10 million per launch.
Isar Aerospace is backed by ESA's 'Boost!' programme, which supports European commercial launch vehicle development.
The first Spectrum test flight in March 2025 flew for 30 seconds, clearing the launch pad and proving the rocket could achieve liftoff.

stories.headline: Rocket Lab Scrubs ESA Celeste LEO Navigation Satellite Launch Due to Weather

key_facts.fact: Weather conditions over Launch Complex 1 in Mahia, New Zealand violated cloud and lightning commit criteria, forcing Rocket Lab to stand down from the Celeste mission on March 25.
A weather system passing through the region means the next target launch date will be set once it clears, likely a delay of several days.

The 'Daughter of the Stars' mission would deploy two IOD satellites to 510 km LEO orbit as part of ESA's Celeste program to test LEO Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (LEO-PNT) technology complementing the Galileo system.
The Celeste constellation will eventually comprise 11 satellites testing innovative signals across multiple frequencies to boost European navigation resilience and performance.
The two IOD spacecraft were built by Thales Alenia Space and GMV, Europe's satellite navigation prime contractors.

stories.headline: SpaceX Launches 54 Starlink Satellites in Two Back-to-Back Missions Within 9 Hours

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched 25 Starlink V2 Mini satellites from Vandenberg SFB on a Falcon 9 (Starlink Group 17-17) at approximately 02:39 UTC on March 26, after rescheduling from the previous day.
A second Falcon 9 launched 29 Starlink v2 Mini satellites from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at 11:22 UTC on March 26, roughly 9 hours after the Vandenberg mission.
The Cape Canaveral booster was flying for its 27th time, one of SpaceX's most-flown boosters, having previously launched NASA Crew-6, SES, and USSF missions.
The Cape Canaveral launch was SpaceX's 37th orbital mission of 2026 and the 21st from Florida's Space Coast this year.

stories.headline: China Launches Two SuperView Neo 2 SAR Earth Observation Satellites

key_facts.fact: China launched a Long March 2D rocket carrying SuperView Neo 2-05 and 2-06 commercial synthetic-aperture radar Earth observation satellites at 22:51 UTC on March 25.
The satellites were built by CAST for China Siwei Survey and Mapping Technology Co. Ltd. and deployed to sun-synchronous orbit from Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center.
This was the 66th orbital launch attempt globally in 2026, reflecting a record-setting pace of orbital access worldwide.
It was the second Long March 2D mission of 2026, with the rocket having a 103-mission track record.

stories.headline: Lucid Bots Raises $20M Series B to Scale Autonomous Cleaning Drone Platform

key_facts.fact: Lucid Bots raised an oversubscribed $20 million Series B co-led by Cubit Capital and Idea Fund Partners, bringing total funding to $34 million.
The company's operator network has surpassed $75 million in jobs completed with nearly 1,000 robots deployed nationwide, growing from 100 to 700 units in less than five months.
Lucid Bots launched a power tether option for its Sherpa cleaning drone enabling unlimited flight time, garnering nearly $1 million in pre-orders.

The company launched Lucid Refresh, a Robotics-as-a-Service subscription platform letting operators access drones, the Lavo AI pressure washing robot, fleet software, training, and support without upfront capital.
Funding will scale commercial operations, expand domestic manufacturing in Charlotte, NC, and accelerate product rollout including the new Lavo AI autonomous ground-based pressure washing robot.

stories.headline: Ukrainian OSIRIS AI Unveils Combat-Tested UEB-1 AI Interceptor Drone at 315 km/h

key_facts.fact: OSIRIS AI presented the UEB-1 interceptor drone at the Xpotential 2026 exhibition in Dusseldorf, Germany, designed to intercept high-speed aerial targets at up to 315 km/h.
The drone uses the OSIRIS DroneOS platform with AI for autonomous trajectory prediction and object tracking, requiring minimal operator involvement.
Specs include 18 km flight range, 10+ minutes endurance, 3.1 kg total weight with 0.5 kg payload, and a carbon fiber frame measuring 370 x 370 x 550 mm.
The drone has been tested in combat conditions and is part of the OSIRIS AI ecosystem for countering aerial threats from the Russian Federation.
OSIRIS AI has production facilities in Ukraine and Poland with an R&D center in Krakow, funded by foreign investment received in 2025.

stories.headline: Iran Rejects US 15-Point Ceasefire Plan, Issues Own Five-Point Counterproposal

key_facts.fact: Iran dismissed the US 15-point ceasefire plan on March 25 and issued its own five-point counterproposal via state television
Iran's five demands include: halt to killings of Iranian officials, security guarantees against future wars, reparations for damages, end of hostilities, and sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz
A senior Iranian military spokesperson stated: 'People like us can never get along with people like you... no one like us will make a deal with you. Not now. Not ever.'
Mediators are pursuing in-person talks, potentially Friday in Pakistan, though significant obstacles remain due to unclear authority within Iran's government and deep mutual distrust
War death toll stands at Iran 1,500+, Israel 20 (including 2 soldiers in Lebanon), US military 13+, Lebanon nearly 1,100, Iraq 80 security force members

stories.headline: Iranian Drones Hit Kuwait International Airport Fuel Tank, Sparking Major Fire

key_facts.fact: Drones struck a fuel tank at Kuwait International Airport on March 25, triggering a fire that sent huge plumes of smoke over the area
Kuwait's Directorate General of Civil Aviation reported only 'limited damage' with no casualties from the strike
Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed responsibility, stating they launched missiles and drones at military bases hosting US forces in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain
The airport has been largely closed to commercial flights since the regional war began on February 28, with previous attacks on March 8 and March 14

stories.headline: Russian Drone Strikes Damage Lviv's UNESCO World Heritage Center

key_facts.fact: Russian drones struck Lviv's historic city center on March 25, damaging buildings in the UNESCO World Heritage-listed area including the Bernardine Monastery complex
Several people were injured in the strikes, with emergency services deploying to contain fires in the historic center
Other Ukrainian regions including Donetsk and Vinnytsia also reported strikes and casualties on the same day
Russia continued launching hundreds of drones at Ukraine on March 25 as part of its spring offensive, following a record barrage of nearly 1,000 in the preceding days

stories.headline: Oil Prices Plunge 4% as Trump Signals Iran Peace Talks Despite Tehran Denial

key_facts.fact: WTI crude fell 3.77% to $88.87/barrel and Brent crude dropped 3.9% to $100.40/barrel on March 25
The drop stripped part of a war-driven premium that had boosted oil prices over 30% since the conflict began in late February
Trump said Washington was negotiating with Tehran, while Iran denied direct talks, leaving traders uncertain about ceasefire prospects
Dallas Fed energy survey showed business activity index surging to +21.0 in Q1 2026 from -6.2 in Q4 2025, with company outlook jumping to +32.2 from -15.2
US equity markets rallied: S&P 500 gained 0.7%, Dow Jones rose 0.7%, Nasdaq climbed 1.1%, Russell 2000 up 1.5%

stories.headline: Legal AI Startup Harvey Raises $200M at $11B Valuation Led by GIC and Sequoia

key_facts.fact: Harvey raised $200 million in a growth round at an $11 billion valuation, co-led by GIC and Sequoia Capital
Additional investors include Andreessen Horowitz, Coatue, Conviction Partners, Elad Gil, Evantic, and Kleiner Perkins
Over 25,000 custom AI agents are currently running on Harvey's platform, serving law firms including Ashurst, Baker Donelson, Cuatrecasas, and GSK Stockmann
The capital will expand custom agent infrastructure and scale embedded legal engineering teams within top law firms and legal departments

stories.headline: FDA Approves Denali's AVLAYAH, First New Hunter Syndrome Treatment in 20 Years

key_facts.fact: FDA approved AVLAYAH (tividenofusp alfa-eknm) on March 25 for neurologic manifestations of Hunter syndrome (MPS II) in pediatric patients, the first new treatment for the disease in nearly 20 years
Phase 1/2 trial of 47 participants showed 91% reduction in cerebrospinal fluid heparan sulfate by week 24, with 93% of patients (41 of 44) achieving normal-range levels
The drug uses Denali's TransportVehicle platform to cross the blood-brain barrier via receptor-mediated transcytosis, delivering enzyme replacement to the central nervous system
Hunter syndrome (MPS II) is a rare lysosomal storage disorder affecting approximately 500 individuals in the US; Denali received a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher

stories.headline: Beam Therapeutics Reports Strong Base Editing Results in Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency

key_facts.fact: BEAM-302, a base editing therapy that directly corrects the PiZ mutation in the SERPINA1 gene, showed mean steady-state AAT levels of 16.1 micromolar, consistently above the 11 micromolar protective threshold
Corrected M-AAT composition reached 94% of total AAT while mutant Z-AAT was reduced by 84% in 29 treated patients
No serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxicities were reported across single doses up to 75 mg, with only mild to moderate adverse events observed
CEO John Evans called BEAM-302 a potential 'first- and best-in-class one-time treatment'; pivotal cohort of ~50 patients expected to begin enrollment in H2 2026 pursuing accelerated approval
